title: The Letters of Port Alder
premise: Edmund Sterling, a widowed single mother running Port Alder's only bookshop, has spent twelve years keeping her heart as carefully shelved as her rarest volumes. When a water-damaged letter postmarked eleven years ago surfaces behind the shop's wallpaper, she learns that Julian Marsh—the man who left town without goodbye—never received her reply, and that he is dying and has returned to find her. As Edmund helps Julian finish his last wish, cataloguing his late grandmother's letters into a book, their old love rekindles against her fear of losing again and her daughter's quiet resistance to change. In the end, Edmund chooses to risk the whole heart: Julian's illness stabilizes rather than resolves neatly, and they build an imperfect, present-tense family together in Port Alder.
about_author: Quentin Ravensworth is the pen name of a former coastal bookseller who spent a decade writing love letters for strangers at a seaside stall before turning to fiction. Ravensworth writes romances about second chances, small towns, and the courage it takes to be known.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ordinary Days
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. We meet Edmund, her daughter Wren, and the rhythms of the bookshop—story hour, regulars, careful routines built after her husband's death. A developer's letter threatens the building with sale. Emotional beat: comfort shadowed by stagnation; Edmund mistakes safety for peace.

chapters.title: Behind the Wallpaper
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Repairing a burst pipe, Edmund peels back shop wallpaper and finds a yellowed envelope addressed to her, postmarked eleven years ago—her own unsent words to Julian Marsh, returned undelivered. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past knocking through plaster.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian arrives in Port Alder gaunt from treatment, carrying his grandmother's trunk of letters and one purpose: finding Edmund before time runs out. He watches the bookshop lights from the harbor wall, unable yet to walk in. Emotional beat: longing braided with shame and mortality.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The confrontation: Julian explains he left after her husband's funeral out of guilt; the lost letter proves she had asked him to stay. Old wounds reopen in the shop's back room while Wren eavesdrops on the stairs. Emotional beat: grief colliding with hope, neither winning.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Archive
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Julian proposes they co-curate his grandmother Ada's sixty years of letters into a book—a project with a deadline tied to his prognosis. Edmund agrees, telling herself it's professional. Emotional beat: cautious re-entry; love disguised as work.

chapters.title: Wren's Winter
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Twelve-year-old Wren, fiercely loyal to her father's memory, resents Julian's presence and acts out—skipping story hour, testing Edmund. Through Ada's letters she secretly reads about a mother's regret. Emotional beat: jealousy softening toward curiosity.

chapters.title: A Letter Never Meant for Me
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Among Ada's papers, Julian finds evidence the developer's offer traces to a family debt—and that Ada once chose duty over love and regretted it for fifty years. His health falters publicly at the harbor festival; Edmund catches him. Emotional beat: fear made flesh; the deadline becomes real.

chapters.title: Lending Pieces
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Hospital vigil. Edmund realizes she has loved everyone in her life in installments, holding back principal against future loss. She and Wren argue bitterly when Edmund admits she wants Julian to stay. Emotional beat: the cost of half-loving named aloud.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. Auction day for the building. Edmund publicly bids everything—including the shop's future—using advance money from Ada's book deal, choosing both Julian and the town over safety. Julian, discharged and furious at being protected, must choose to accept being loved rather than spare her grief by leaving. Emotional beat: mutual surrender; risk fully taken.

chapters.title: Postmarked Today
chapters.summary: Resolution, Edmund's POV with a closing Wren coda. Spring: the shop reopens with Ada's published letters on display; Julian's scans hold steady, uncertain but present. Wren gives Julian a letter of her own—permission, in a child's handwriting. Edmund mails herself a letter to open next year, no longer afraid of what tomorrow says. Emotional beat: found family, chosen daily.
